decisions.decision: Commit Phase 3 bootstrap separately from Phase 3 planning output
decisions.rationale: Two distinct logical units: 'Phase 3 defined as a roadmap entity' vs. 'Phase 3 broken down into executable plans'. Keeping them in separate commits means if planner output needs rework, roadmap/requirements plumbing stays intact.

decisions.decision: Push all 3 local commits before planning (not just the bootstrap commit)
decisions.rationale: Opening brief listed unpushed commits as non-blocking cleanup. Pushing before planning makes the remote a legitimate restore point; deferring creates a 4th unpushed commit for no reason. Branch is tracked, fast-forward only, no force push needed.

plan-phase.md step 4 explicitly says 'Do NOT invoke discuss-phase as a nested Skill/Task call' — it will route to top-level command and exit. Running discuss-phase first avoids wasted steps and produces a higher-fidelity CONTEXT.md for the planner to work from. decisions.decision: User delegated gray-area judgement to Claude with UAT-adaptation notes
decisions.rationale: User: 'I'll defer to your judgement on how we should proceed with all of these gray areas. My gut tells me UAT will make or break any of these decisions and cause us to adapt one way or another.' Claude selected defaults for all 6 gray areas (D-01..D-06) and embedded explicit 'UAT adaptation' subsections in each describing the concrete signal that would flip the decision and the swap cost. Each decision is encapsulated so swaps remain cheap.

decisions.decision: D-01 load point: app.conf/static primary, nav XML fallback, per-dashboard drop-in fallback, admin local/web.conf escalation
decisions.rationale: web.conf ruled out by REQ-DS-07 (no system config from app). Standard Splunk-app static-resource path is primary. Plan 03-01 research must empirically verify which mechanism fires on DS dashboard view pages in splunk-10-dev (research matrix spans Classic SimpleXML / DS listing / DS editor / DS view).

decisions.decision: D-02 presence detection: first-fetch timeout 1500ms per-iframe-latch; ping/pong literals RESERVED but not implemented
decisions.rationale: Ping handshake adds mandatory round-trip on every DS dashboard load. First-fetch timeout pays zero extra cost in the common case (bridge present) and accumulates only ~1.5s delay in the rare case (bridge absent). Ping/pong reserved in the four-type allow-list so a future phase can add active health-checks without re-opening the message-type threat surface.

decisions.decision: D-03 transport: Blob via structured clone (ArrayBuffer fallback, base64 last-resort)
decisions.rationale: Zero encode/decode CPU cost vs base64's 33% inflation; URL.createObjectURL is canonical Leaflet-compatible path; supported in all target browsers (Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge last 2). Schema field name 'tileData' is representation-agnostic so fallbacks don't require schema changes.

decisions.decision: D-04 URL-shape regex: exported constant in ds-tile-proxy-helpers.js + literal copy in parent-auth-bridge.js + Jest drift-guard via marker comments
decisions.rationale: Parent shim is stand-alone Splunk-Web-loaded IIFE; cannot require() Webpack-bundled helper; standing up a second Webpack entry for ~150 LOC is disproportionate. Copy-paste with drift guard is the honest version of sharing. Starting regex is specification intent — Plan 03-01 research must verify empirically against a real UAT-2 captured URL before committing.

decisions.decision: D-05 rate limit: fixed-window counter, 500 req/1000ms, keyed on event.source, silent drop on breach, one warn per breach window, 60s stale-entry GC
decisions.rationale: Fixed window simpler code; 2x boundary burst (1000 tiles/2s) within Splunk Web ceiling. event.source correctly distinguishes multiple Maps+ iframes on the same page (all share origin 'null'). Silent drop denies abuser throttle signal; one-warn-per-window mirrors iframe-side D-15 'one line per problem'. 500/s gives 3-4x headroom over worst-case Leaflet pan-zoom (~120-180 tiles at max zoom 4K).

decisions.decision: D-06 requestId/timeout/in-flight cap: monotonic int per layer; 8s per-request timeout (Phase 1 server timeout 10s - 2s network budget); first-timeout logged, rest suppressed; 256 in-flight cap (matches Phase 1 cache working set)
decisions.rationale: Monotonic int is smallest correlation nonce; zero security purpose so no RNG needed. 8s buffer below Phase 1's 10s upstream timeout. Leaflet cancels tiles on pan/zoom producing legitimate timeout-like events; logging each violates D-15. 256 in-flight cap prevents compromised iframe from opening 100K fetches (DoS): D-05 bounds rate, D-06 bounds concurrency.

decisions.decision: Non-negotiables D-NN-1..D-NN-6 inherited from .continue-here.md BLOCKING anti-patterns
decisions.rationale: D-NN-1 browser boundary not client bug (requires MDN citation in 03-RESEARCH.md); D-NN-2 exactly four message-type literals including ping/pong reserved; D-NN-3 no auth material in payloads with frozen request/response schemas; D-NN-4 exact-origin === validation both ends with Jest negative tests for close-but-not-equal origins; D-NN-5 Phase 1 SSRF allow-list authoritative; D-NN-6 graceful fallback with exactly one warn per iframe lifetime. These are non-negotiable and bind every downstream agent.
